title: Shortburst hedge amplification diagnostic (P0)
content:
Incident overview
-----------------
Incident ID: SRE-14567
Severity: P0
Event window: 2030-05-09 03:14 UTC -> 2030-05-09 05:22 UTC (mitigations ongoing through 05-12)
Short summary: A short, high-rate burst from an internal onboarding batch job combined with an aggressive client-side hedging policy produced a multiplicative amplification of traffic. The amplification saturated ephemeral headroom on edge proxies, caused acceptor/backlog growth in the multiplexing layer, and triggered widespread streaming session resets and 5xx errors across hosted API front-end clusters.

Impact
------
- Affected surface: hosted-api public endpoints (generation + streaming) in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for ~128 minutes at peak.
- Error types: 5xx spike (primarily 503, 524-like timeouts from upstream), streaming fragmentation and session reinitializations, TTFB p95/p99 latency > 10x baseline.
- Customer impact: approx 9% of production requests failed at peak; streaming session drop rate increased from 0.2% -> 6.8%. Several high-volume customers reported elevated error rates and partial feature degradation.
- Business impact: temporary SLA exposure for paid Dedicated customers during the 30-minute max-surge window (we issued customer comms).

Detection and timeline (UTC)
---------------------------
- 03:14: alerting: hosted-api p98 latency alert fired (oncall mobile push).
- 03:15: SRE pager -> join incident channel; initial dashboards show TTFB spike in us-west-2.
- 03:20: error rate climbs, 5xx pattern appears; oncall collects traces and spikes in hedging metrics (hedge_count metric jumping).
- 03:26: SRE suspects traffic amplification; engineering toggles additional telemetry for per-tenant inbound rates.
- 03:40: source identified: internal onboarding batch job (job-id: onboarding-regen-2030-05-09-03) began a retry loop hitting API with short-lived connections and small payloads.
- 03:47: manual mitigation 1: kill offending job and apply immediate token-based rate-limiter for that job. Error rates drop but streaming instability persists.
- 04:02: mitigation 2: disable client hedging at the edge as temporary measure (hedging contributed to multifanout). Streaming reconnects begin but p99 latency remains elevated.
- 04:45: manual horizontal scale: increase front-end pool headroom and bring up warm nodes; queueing drains.
- 05:22: observable health returns to near-baseline; monitoring and small mitigations continue into the day.

Immediate root cause (synthesized)
----------------------------------
Root cause is multi-factor and emergent:
1) A scheduled internal batch job entered a retry loop (bug in backoff) and generated a short, high-rate burst of many concurrent short-lived requests aimed at the hosted API.
2) Edge hedging logic (configured to secure latency SLOs by launching hedged requests) treated the short-lived request failures/slow responses as candidate hedges and launched additional parallel requests.
3) Hedging + the short-lived retry traffic multiplied total ingress into the front-end pool ~3-7x the original burst, which consumed ephemeral connection/headroom resources and produced headroom exhaustion on edge proxies.
4) As headroom decreased, acceptor queues in the multiplexing layer grew; the scheduler attempted to shed load by throttling and applying circuit breakers, but configuration thresholds were too conservative and kicked in too late.
5) Streaming sessions are sensitive to mid-request connection resets; reinitialization logic caused chunked responses to fragment and client-side reconnect noise to further magnify load.

Contributing systemic factors
----------------------------
- No per-job quota enforcement for internal onboarding jobs; internal jobs run with broad API tokens.
- Hedging threshold math was tuned aggressively toward latency SLOs without a safety multiplier for headroom or for short high-rate patterns.
- Telemetry lacked real-time per-API-key ingress rate dashboards; we were blind to the origin of the burst for ~11 minutes.
- Autoscaler cooldown is conservative and did not react to short bursts; warm pools were insufficient for sudden fanout.
- Runbook lacked a concise, tested procedure for "hedging amplification" scenarios (we had partial notes but no button to quickly disable hedging globally).

Evidence collected
------------------
- Aggregated logs: spike of requests with user-agent "onboarding-processor/2.1" and token prefix ONB- at 03:14:05 UTC.
- Hedging metric: hedge_count rose from baseline 1.02 -> 3.8 concurrently with ingress spike.
- Connection telemetry: ephemeral-sockets-in-use on edge proxies saturated at 96% capacity at 03:28.
- Traces: example trace id trace-0a1b2c3d showed 4 parallel hedged attempts before final success; p95 tail latencies increased in these traces.

In-incident mitigations (what we did)
------------------------------------
1) Kill offending internal job and revoke the token used by that job. (Aisha P., 03:47)
2) Apply a temporary token-scoped rate limit for internal batch tokens to 10 r/s per token. (Marco L., 03:50)
3) Disable hedging at edge for hosted-api route (toggle via feature-flag). (SRE lead, 04:02)
4) Increase front-end headroom by adding warm nodes and relaxing headroom reservation for streaming; this reduced queueing. (Infra team, 04:20)
5) Gradually re-enable hedging with a safety multiplier and monitor. (04:50 -> 05:22)

What prevented faster resolution
--------------------------------
- We lacked an automated quick-flip for hedging; the disable took manual approval and feature-flag propagation across regions (added ~8 minutes).
- Per-token rate limits are too permissive for some internal systems; no running guardrails prevented onboarding job from accelerating aggressively.
- The telemetry gap meant we had to instrument additional metrics mid-incident which delayed definitive source identification.

Post-incident action items (owners + proposed deadlines)
-------------------------------------------------------
1) Create per-token/job quota enforcement path in the API gateway (owner: Priya S., due: 2030-05-20).
2) Add a hedging safety multiplier: if ephemeral_headroom < 30% then hedging factor must not exceed 1.2 (owner: Marco L., due: 2030-05-16).
3) Implement a global "hedging emergency flip" in the control plane that is region-propagated within 5s (owner: Devon O'Neal, due: 2030-06-01).
4) Dashboard: add per-API-key ingress rate and an alert when a single key is > 2x baseline for > 60s (owner: SRE observability, Renee T., due: 2030-05-13).
5) Autoscaler policy review: add a short-burst scaling path and reduce warm-up cooldown for front-ends for sudden fanout patterns (owner: infra-scaling, owner: TBD, due: 2030-05-30).
6) Runbook authoring: draft and test a "hedge-amplification" page with playbook steps (owner: Aisha P., due: 2030-05-15).
7) Create an internal ticket to audit all long-lived internal tokens and apply least-privilege / per-job tokens (owner: Security, due: 2030-06-10).

Runbook draft (condensed)
------------------------
Title: Hedge amplification / sudden-fanout emergency response\- Step 0: Triage and scope: check ingress-by-key and hedge_count metrics.\- Step 1: If a single API key > 2x baseline for > 60s, immediately mark incidents and apply token rate limit.\- Step 2: If hedge_count > 2 and ephemeral_headroom < 40% -> consider hedging emergency flip.\- Step 3: Scale up front-end warm pool if headroom < 50% and scaling available.\- Step 4: If streaming fragmentation persists after killing source and scaling, temporarily disable streaming rejoin heuristics for affected region.\- Step 5: After stabilization, re-enable hedging with conservative factor and monitor for 30m.
Notes: include simple scripts to find top-10 tokens by QPS, a one-click feature-flag page, and links to kill internal jobs via orchestration UI.

Follow-ups already created
-------------------------
- JIRA SRE-14568: implement hedging emergency flip (link above).
- JIRA INF-2762: add per-token ingress dashboard and alerts.
- JIRA SRE-14569: runbook test and tabletop exercise scheduling.

Open questions / unresolved
-------------------------
- What is the best automatic heuristic to bound hedging when ephemeral resources are constrained? (automatic headroom-aware multiplier vs. simple global cap)
- Should some internal jobs be required to run through a dedicated internal-gateway with stricter caps?
- Can autoscaler be tuned to detect hedging-amplified signals vs. organic traffic spikes without overprovisioning?

Notes to self / informal observations
-----------------------------------
- Hedging bought latency for small fractions but cost us overall availability when combined with retry storms.
- Need a chaos test that simulates a background job retry storm while hedging is enabled.
- The one-minute telemetry blindspot was the biggest friction — prioritize real-time per-key rates.

Appendix (quick links and logs)
------------------------------
- key example trace: trace-0a1b2c3d (hedged attempt sequence)
- log snippet: onboarding-regen-2030-05-09-03 -> repeated 401/429/timeout then retry backoff failed (attached in JIRA INF-2762)
- slack transcript: #sre-incident/T03ABCD1234-incident-log (channel pinned)

TL;DR
-----
A buggy internal batch job produced a short burst. Our hedging system multiplied the load, headroom was exhausted on edge proxies, and acceptor queueing led to streaming fragmentation and broad 5xxs. Mitigations: kill job, token rate-limit, disable hedging, scale pools. Action items: per-token quotas, hedging safety multipliers, hedging emergency flip, improved telemetry and runbook tests.

Draft notes end.
